correctness.rationale: For all n,m the independent Poisson embedding makes the last mth event unique and the other n-1 exact-m indicators conditionally independent, giving the stated binomial mixture. The Gamma upper-tail quantile has (b-m)/sqrt(m)->infinity; the exact tail/density integral yields w~b/(b-m) and marked ratio p_m/Q_m~b/m-1 on its local Gumbel window. Conditional Poisson mixing yields Geom and variance control yields normalized Exp. Gamma Chernoff/Cramer rates give the logarithmic phase parameter. The original discrete process is identical in ordered marks. Standalone two-method rational checker passes 143 assertions; it does not replace analytic infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact m=1 terminal singleton distribution is due to Myers and Wilf, and completion-time Gumbel limits are due to Castro–Marinho and Long. The new non-implied observable is the number of bins at precisely the growing threshold at the *random m-fold completion time*, with an explicit transition on m/log n and an all-sequence conditional marked-clocking proof. Closest published work on delayed deficits and fixed levels (Ilienko) does not itself state this growing-multiplicity geometric family. Search does not establish absolute priority; possible broader marked point-process coverage remains a listed risk.
residual_risks: An older general marked-extremes or Poisson occupancy process theorem might subsume the growing-m_n result despite the lack of a directly located statement.
Full appendices of Castro–Marinho 2026 were not available on repeated arXiv HTML requests; source comparison is therefore bounded.
Some fixed-threshold limits can already follow from Ilienko and Myers–Wilf; novelty is specifically the logarithmic growing-threshold family.

value.rationale: The minimally filled count at the moment all coupon quotas have just been reached measures the number of remaining bottleneck types in repeated coverage. The exact changing-quota phase transition at m_n/asymp log n with continuum of geometric laws is a natural structural invariant beyond the total stopping time and gives a concrete phase diagram. Exact integral enables independent finite-size validation; no downstream sweeping claim is required.
